# IFC test fixtures plan

Status: curated standalone fixture corpus used by IFC codec, validation, and geometry tests.
Last updated: 2026-08-25

This is task state, not ambient context. Follow `AGENTS.md` and load this file
only when changing the fixture corpus.

## Established boundary

Small synthetic or minimal upstream IFC files with preserved provenance.

## Planned file map

- `ifclite-geometry/`: geometry and processing edge cases.
- `ifcopenshell-validate/`: schema/header validation cases.
- `costing/`: local costing round-trip fixture.

## `synthetic-compile/` — authored here, not upstream

`union_over_halfspace_unbounded.ifc`, derived from
`ifclite-geometry/issue_1155_halfspace_flyaway.ifc` by retyping
`IFCBOOLEANCLIPPINGRESULT(.DIFFERENCE.,...)` to `IFCBOOLEANRESULT(.UNION.,...)`.
Not byte-identical to upstream, so it must never move into
`ifclite-geometry/`, whose provenance rule requires exactly that.

Difference and intersection stay inside the finite left operand, so a prism
covering its bounds is an exact stand-in -- which is why `issue_1155`
compiles. Union escapes that bound and the reference compiler refuses.
The file validates clean: the refusal belongs to the mesh provider, not the
file. It keeps the refusal branch of `ifc-geometry/tests/compile_pairing.rs`
executable; a mutation run confirmed that branch is dead code without it.

- vertex_loop_zero_area.ifc: derived from shared_point_faceted_brep.ifc by
  replacing one IfcPolyLoop face bound with an IfcVertexLoop. Proves the
  degenerate zero-area loop reports a typed refusal naming the entity,
  not a wrong-type error that reads as a corrupt file.

## `synthetic-surfaces/` — per-file rationale

Moved from `AGENTS.md` to keep ambient context under its line cap.

Generated by [`../../tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py`](../../tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py)
using ifcopenshell 0.8.5. **Not sourced from any upstream corpus**, and that
is deliberate: no licensed public corpus we surveyed carries curved or
B-spline surfaces at all. `ifc-lite` (MPL-2.0) has none; the buildingSMART
sets (CC-BY-4.0) contain only faceted breps and extrusions; the one repo that
does have them, `IfcOpenShell/files`, publishes **no licence**, so its files
cannot be redistributed here. Generating our own is the only route that is
both licence-clean and committable.

Covers `IfcCylindricalSurface`, `IfcSphericalSurface`, `IfcToroidalSurface`,
`IfcSurfaceOfRevolution`, `IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface`,
`IfcBSplineSurfaceWithKnots`, and `IfcCurveBoundedPlane`, plus
`IfcAdvancedBrep` (`synthetic_advanced_brep.ifc`: a half-cylinder plug whose
three faces share four edges through eight `IfcOrientedEdge` uses, with one
`IfcEdgeCurve` and one `IfcAdvancedFace` authored `SameSense=.F.` so a
dropped flag is observable), `IfcRectangularPyramid` and
`IfcBoundingBox` (`synthetic_primitives_and_bbox.ifc`: three distinct
extents, so a slot-order mistake cannot pass), and the loose collections
(`synthetic_collections.ifc`: a curve set of a polyline plus a circle, and
a shell-based surface model of two triangles in an OPEN shell — it must
never acquire a volume), the tapered and variable-section sweeps
(`synthetic_tapered_sweeps.ifc`: every tapered pair uses DISTINCT start and
end profiles so reusing `SweptArea` for both ends is observable, the
revolution angle is authored in degrees, the fixed reference is `+Z` rather
than the `+X` a lowerer would default to, and the polygonal disk appears
BOTH with and without `FilletRadius`, so a dropped fillet is observable), and `IfcSectionedSpine` (`synthetic_sectioned_spine.ifc`: three
different profiles at three distinct stations along a composite curve).
All are authored in
**millimetres with degree angles** — the combination that catches a unit
factor applied to the wrong quantity kind — and every file passes
`ifcopenshell.validate` with zero issues.

Regenerate with:

```
python3 tools/gen_surface_fixtures.py test/fixtures/synthetic-surfaces
```

Edit the generator, never the `.ifc` output: the script is the source of
truth and records why each value was chosen (e.g. the revolution axis sits
off-origin so a missing millimetre conversion cannot hide).
